newsitem.title: USA: Service says committed to Loewen deal.
newsitem.headline: Service says committed to Loewen deal.

text.p: Service Corp International said it is committed to a transaction with rival Loewen Group Inc and has scheduled a board meeting for October 1 to review its options.
Loewen last night rejected Service Corp's unsolicited takeover bid of $43 per share, or $2.8 billion.

"We are disappointed that the Loewen board of directors rejected our proposals without ever returning our calls or seeking more information from us. The actions of the Loewen board simply deprive its stockholders of the oppportunity to receive prompt value for their shareholders," said Service chairman Robert Waltrip.
Service Corp disclosed its offer last week and indicated it would be willing to raise the bid if Loewen granted it access to its financial records.
Loewen rejected the offer after meeting for about seven hours yesterday, saying it intends to remain independent.
Service Corp and Loewen are the nation's two largest operators of funeral homes and cemeteries.
Service Corp said its stock offer represents a 48.9 percent premium over the price Loewen stock was trading at 30 days before its offer.

With the rejection, Service Corp must now decide whether it will raise its offer or pursue a hostile takeover of Loewen. Analysts have said that Service may have a difficult time winning Loewen on a hostile basis because chief executive officer Raymond Loewen holds about 15 percent of the firm's common shares and insiders hold about another three percent.
A hostile takeover would require the approval of 75 percent of voting Loewen holders.
